ARI promotes scientific waste management and sustainable gardening under swachhata special campaign 6.0
articles.full_content:
As part of the Special Campaign 6.0, the Agharkar Research Institute (ARI), Pune, is promoting scientific organic waste management, nutrient recycling and sustainable maintenance of green spaces across its campus. The Institute produces approximately 6,000 kg of compost annually from fallen leaves and garden waste and utilises it in its gardens. This initiative converts organic waste into a valuable soil amendment, promotes resource conservation and demonstrates the practical application of circular economy principles by returning organic matter and nutrients to the soil.
Fig 1: Fallen leaves and palm fronds decomposing on the ARI campus, returning organic matter to the soil.
At ARI, fallen leaves and other garden residues are collected, crushed into smaller pieces and placed in a designated compost pit for in-house composting. The material is mixed weekly to facilitate aeration and microbial decomposition. Mature compost is harvested after approximately three to four months and used in the Institute’s gardens. During composting, microorganisms break down complex organic materials into more stable organic matter.
Fig 2: Compost pits at ARI, Pune, where fallen leaves and garden residues are composted in-house.
At ARI, a mixture comprising 80% compost and 20% soil is used for gardening helping improve soil structure, enhancing water-holding capacity, contributing to soil organic matter and supporting nutrient availability for plants. The annual production and on-site utilisation of compost facilitate the productive reuse of locally available organic resources and help reduce the need for externally purchased gardening inputs. It also reduces the volume of garden waste requiring disposal and supports more resource-efficient campus management. On-site composting may further reduce waste transportation and the environmental impacts associated with landfill disposal.
ARI maintains approximately two acres of gardens and green areas, contributing to plant diversity, biodiversity conservation and the environmental quality of the campus. The Garden Section maintains approximately 308 trees representing more than 100 species, 39 medicinal plant species, 2,300 ornamental plants and 800 seasonal flowering plants, along with a variety of vegetables. The Institute’s Orchidarium supports the conservation and display of orchid diversity and facilitates specialised plant conservation and educational activities. The maintenance of diverse trees, medicinal plants and ornamental vegetation strengthens the campus’s green infrastructure and promotes awareness of plant diversity and conservation.
Complementing its waste management initiatives, ARI promotes nutrition-sensitive horticulture through its 6×6 Nutrition Garden Model. Designed for a compact area of 6 × 6 metres, the model demonstrates the cultivation of 23 types of vegetables through systematic crop planning and efficient utilisation of available space. NDRF Academy, Nagpur, operationalises 500 kW solar power plant to promote clean energy
articles.full_content:
Nagpur, 23 October 2026
The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) Academy, Nagpur, operationalised a 500 kW solar power plant at its Suradevi campus on October 22, 2026, marking a significant step towards promoting renewable energy and sustainable campus operations.
The project has been completed under the initiative of the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI), in alignment with the Government of India’s vision of expanding clean energy use and reducing dependence on conventional power sources.
The inauguration ceremony was presided over by Commandant (Works) BS Rajput of NDRF Academy, Nagpur. The officials associated with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL), Nagpur, and officers and personnel of the Academy were also present.
The 500 kW solar power plant is expected to contribute significantly to meeting the campus’s electricity requirements through renewable energy, enhance energy efficiency and reduce dependence on conventional grid power.
The commissioning of the plant reflects coordinated efforts by the NDRF Academy, the implementing agency and electricity distribution authorities to promote clean energy adoption. The initiative marks an important milestone in the Academy’s efforts to develop an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable campus, in keeping with national priorities of renewable energy promotion and environmental protection.
PIB Nagpur | Saurabh Khekde/Darshana Rane

Chairman, CBIC Holds Trade Interaction Meeting in Mumbai on GST Reforms and Ease of Doing Business
articles.full_content:
Mumbai, 23 October 2026
As part of Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) continued nation-wide outreach following the 57th GST Council meeting held on 8 Oct 2026, a Trade Interaction was organized today by the Central Goods & Services Tax (CGST) & Central Excise, Mumbai zone in Mumbai. Approximately 150 representatives from taxpayers, various trade associations and chambers across Maharashtra attended the event.
The meeting was chaired by Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, in the presence of Shri Sanjay Mangal, Member (GST), CBIC, Ms. Prachi Saroop, Principal Chief Commissioner, CGST & Central Excise, Mumbai Zone and Shri Asheesh Sharma, Commissioner of State Tax, State GST, Maharashtra. Senior officers of the Central and State GST administrations, and representatives of leading trade associations and industry bodies were present.
Discussions centred on the recent recommendations of the 57th GST Council Meeting and key developments in the GST framework. Some of the reforms discussed included simplified registration, faster system-based processing of refunds without officer intervention, simplified returns, measures to reduce litigation, streamlined procedures for inter-state movement of goods and easier compliance for small sellers and exporters. Measures like withdrawal of arrest powers and increasing threshold for prosecution to reduce coercion and foster a partnership between taxpayers and government were also highlighted.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, emphasised on the underlying philosophy of “trust first, verify later” behind the next-generation process reforms. He highlighted the council’s resolve to improve the taxpayer experience, reduce friction points and promote ease of doing business.
Shri Sanjay Mangal, Member, CBIC highlighted various measures being undertaken by the Board to make compliance easier. He further added that changes brought in the GST council meeting would be brought in phases and relevant circulars and notifications would be issued in due course.
Shri Asheesh Sharma, Commissioner, State GST, also interacted with the taxpayers and underlined the importance of building trust between taxpayers and the department. He highlighted the steps being taken to reduce physical interception and increase trust.
Industry representatives shared their queries and offered suggestions on a range of GST-related issues. Senior officers responded to the queries raised and assured that the suggestions received would be duly examined.
The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of the GST administration to a responsive, transparent and taxpayer-friendly tax administration, with continued focus on voluntary compliance and ease of doing business.
PIB Mumbai | Nitin Fulluke/Darshana Rane

Changes in PLFS schedule and estimation procedure from January 2027 - inviting comments thereon
articles.full_content:
NSO to introduce changes in PLFS from January 2027
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), has been conducting the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) since 2017. PLFS has evolved to meet the demand for more timely and disaggregated labour market statistics. The sampling design of PLFS was revamped from January 2025 to provide monthly, quarterly and annual estimates and to enable estimation of indicators at sub-state level. Education and skilling questions were added, and also information on digital platform workers, a subset of gig workers, has been collected on an experimental basis since January 2026.
The NSO proposes to introduce modification in the sampling design of the PLFS from January 2027, when fresh samples for the two-year period 2027-2028 (new Panel 6) will be drawn from an updated sampling frame. It also introduces certain changes in the survey schedule. A concept note giving the details has been prepared and is available at https://www.mospi.gov.in/ .
Comments and suggestions are invited from the policymakers, researchers, academic and research institutions and members of the general public on the proposed modifications within 15 days from the date of publication of this press note.
Key changes in sampling design and estimation
• Separate stratum for digital platform workers. Experience from PLFS 2026 showed that the existing arrangement did not capture an adequate number of digital platform workers. A new Second Stage Stratum (SSS) based on digital platform work is being introduced, while the existing SSS structure and composition are retained. There will be four SSSs in rural areas and five in urban areas, with 14 households canvassed in each selected First Stage Unit (FSU). This revision in SSS formation is expected to improve the coverage of digital platform workers and facilitate more comprehensive data collection on this emerging segment of the labour market.
• Updated sampling frame and refinements. Fresh samples for the two-year period 2027-2028 (Panel 6) will be drawn from an updated frame reflecting the updated Urban Frame Survey, urbanisation and de-urbanisation, and the creation, splitting or merger of districts and other administrative units, along with follow-up updation of the rural Census 2011 frame. The updated sampling frame will ensure better representation of the current population, urban population in particular, by capturing changes in urbanisation, administrative boundaries and the emergence of new urban areas. It is expected to improve sample coverage and enhance the reliability and relevance of PLFS estimates.
Additionally, criteria for sample allocation and stratification have also been modified/ updated based on the experience of the previous two-year period (Panel 5). These revisions are expected to improve the efficiency of sample allocation and stratification and ensure better representation of population variations which in turn minimise opera

DDWS Organises National-level Training of Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 to Strengthen Community-led Rural Drinking Water Management
articles.full_content:
Story-based capacity-building package launched to strengthen grassroots leadership and sustainable management of village water supply systems
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised a National-level Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for State-Level Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 today at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. The programme brought together representatives from State Institutes of Rural Development (SIRDs), Public Health Engineering Departments (PHEDs), Rural Development institutions and other key stakeholders from State/UTs to strengthen capacities for large-scale community training and institutional development aimed at sustaining rural drinking water services across the country.
The training programme focused on the newly developed Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 Capacity Building Package comprising of 8 Modules titled “The Story of Panipur: A Story-Based self-learning Handbook on Rural Drinking Water Supply Management” and a “ Trainer’s Facilitation Manual ”. The package has been designed to build the capacities of Gram Panchayat representatives, Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), Sujalam Shakti Groups and other grassroots institutions involved in the management and sustainability of rural drinking water services.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission , stressed that the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems depends fundamentally on community ownership and institutional responsibility. The drinking water infrastructure being created today is intended to serve rural communities for the next several decades and therefore requires active participation of GPs, VWSCs and community groups from the very beginning.
He emphasised that achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 would require not only creation of infrastructure but also sustained efforts to ensure its effective operation and maintenance through strong local institutions.
Referring to emerging examples of improved service delivery in several States, Shri Soan highlighted the need to prepare village institutions for progressively higher service standards and sustainable management of water supply systems. He urged participants to instil a strong sense of ownership among Panchayat representatives and community institutions so that drinking water infrastructure is viewed as a community asset that must be preserved and maintained collectively.
A key focus of his address was the convergence of JJM with Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), Panchayati Raj Institutions, Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) and dovetail from 16th Finance Commission tied grants and VB-G RAM G. Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chairs 30th Meeting of Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) in New Delhi, today
articles.full_content:
FSDC reviews macro-financial stability amid rising geopolitical uncertainties, AI boom and sharp rise in global bond yields FSDC stresses heightened vigilance and proactive measures to mitigate emerging risks to India’s financial stability Union Finance Minister calls for more frequent FSDC meetings amid global economic uncertainties FSDC deliberates on strengthening domestic investment ecosystem, enhancing capital flows and deepening financial sector reforms
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 30 th Meeting of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) along with FSDC members in New Delhi, today.
The FSDC, inter alia, deliberated on issues related to macro financial stability and India’s preparedness to deal with them. Considering the importance of regulatory improvisation and digital modernization in the financial sector, the FSDC discussed measures towards promoting innovation in the Fintech sector and exploring the prospects of tokenisation of financial assets and other real-world assets.
The Council reviewed the cyber resilience of the Indian financial sector and took note of the Financial Sector Cyber Security Strategy (FSCSS) formulated by an Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG) comprising of financial sector regulators and cybersecurity agencies, in coordination with the DEA, DFS and MeitY. The implementation of the FSCSS is expected to strengthen the overall resilience of the Indian financial sector. The discussions also covered India’s preparedness to protect the Critical Information Infrastructure and resilience of protection systems and improving cybersecurity preparedness of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs).
The FSDC also discussed issues relating to formulating a strategy for implementing the past decisions and the budget announcements, which included:
• strengthening the domestic investment ecosystem and improve resource flow for investment including in the GIFT-IFSC;
• simplification and digitalization of the KYC processes and digital onboarding for NRIs and FPIs;
• reforms to scale up DPIs in India including the Account Aggregator and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) framework with specific focus on MSMEs;
• reducing cost of intermediation in the financial sector, improving the responsiveness of regulations and rationalization of Credit Guarantee Schemes in India.
The FSDC took cognizance of the emerging trends from domestic and global macro-financial situation and stressed upon the need to be vigilant especially in view of the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, AI boom and steep rise in global bond yields. The Council recognised the need for proactive efforts to mitigate potential risks to financial stability while adopting adequate safeguards for financial system’s resilience. The members decided to strengthen the inter-regulatory coordination for wider development of the financial sector.

At CII conference, Union Environment Minister calls for coordinated efforts by Government, Industry and Urban Local Bodies to advance India’s Circular Economy
articles.full_content:
Government translating Policy Intent into Meaningful Action through Clear Policies and Regulatory Reforms: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today addressed the Circular Economy Conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in New Delhi. He highlighted India’s efforts to translate policy intent into meaningful action through clear policies, regulatory reforms, digital compliance systems and a whole-of-government approach to advance the circular economy.
Addressed the @FollowCII Circular Economy Conference in Delhi today. Elaborated on how India under the leadership of Hon'ble PM Shri @narendramodi ji has adopted a 'whole of government' approach in creating an enabling platform for all stakeholders to push circular economy. With clear policy, directions like Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 and EPR framewor, the focus now is on translating policy intent into meaningful action. Happy to note that as of October 12, 2026, more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers are registered under various EPR frameworks. Through these collective efforts, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with over 435.043 lakh metric tonnes covered through EPR certificate generation.
In his address, Shri Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Union Government had progressively strengthened the legal framework governing waste management by introducing sector-specific rules for nine waste streams: plastic waste, battery waste, e-waste, waste tyres, used oil, end-of-life vehicles, construction and demolition waste, non-ferrous scrap metal and solid waste. These rules focused on waste prevention, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing and resource recovery across the product lifecycle. The Minister also highlighted that as on date, nearly 499.60 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed across regulated waste streams, with more than 86,043 producers and 4,880 recyclers registered under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks.
Highlighting the role of EPR, the Minister said that the framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to ensure environmentally sound management of products at the end of their life. The transfer of EPR certificates provided financial incentives to recyclers, encouraging capacity expansion, technological advancement and increased recycling, while contributing to job creation and livelihoods across the recycling value chain. Shri Yadav emphasised that regulation alone could not create a circular economy and highlighted the importance of Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative, which calls for mindful and deliberate resource utilisation instead of destructive consumption.

He highlighted India’s efforts to translate policy intent into meaningful action through clear policies, regulatory reforms, digital compliance systems and a whole-of-government approach to advance the circular economy. Addressed the @FollowCII Circular Economy Conference in Delhi today.

articles.full_content:
MoSPI Organizes One-Day Cleanliness Drive under Special Campaign 6.0
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), and its attached and subordinate offices, organized a dedicated One-Day Cleanliness Drive on 7th October, 2026 as part of Special Campaign 6. The initiative focused on improving workplace cleanliness, promoting environmental sustainability, ensuring responsible waste management and facilitating the efficient utilization of office space.
MoSPI conducted comprehensive cleanliness drives across identified three spots around K.L. Bhawan, including Tolstoy Lane, the K.L. Bhawan campus and Janpath Road.
The Field Operations Division (FOD) undertook cleanliness and space-management activities in its Regional Offices and Sub-Regional Offices spread across the country, focusing on better utilization of office space and recognizing the contributions of Safai Mitras. As a part of one day activities, cleanliness drives were conducted at around 53 sites.
Household Survey Division (HSD) and Enterprise Survey Division (EnSD), Kolkata, subordinate offices of MoSPI undertook the cleanliness drive and planted saplings at Mahalanobis Bhavan, Kolkata alongside initiatives for bio-waste segregation. National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) conducted a Swachhata drive in CPWD areas, while Data Informatics & Innovation Division (DIID) organized cleanliness activities at a public park in R.K. Puram, New Delhi and its office premises.
Cleaning at a Public Park (DIID) Cleaning of Solar Panels (NSSTA)
The Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata also undertook a cleanliness drive at its 203 and 205 B.T. Road campuses, removing and disposing of waste to create additional space for campus beautification. A tree plantation drive was organized to enhance greenery and promote environmental sustainability. As part of its e-waste management initiative, electronic items and hardware collected from various departments were segregated and categorized for disposal through e-auction by the Disposal Committee.
Plantation drive (ISI) Segregation of e waste (ISI)
MoSPI is actively participating in Special Campaign 6 by taking measures focused on cleanliness, efficient space management, environmental sustainability and the dignity of sanitation workers.

Towards Future-Ready Data Leaders: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI
articles.full_content:
The chairman of the Committee for Reforming Capacity Building of the Indian Statistical Service (ISS), Sh. P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) submitted the Committee's report to Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI. This marks an important milestone toward strengthening the capacity-building framework for ISS officers. The Committee comprised senior MoSPI officers, knowledge partners, and industry experts.
The Committee reviewed existing ISS training programmes, identified emerging capacity building requirements, and recommended future-oriented training aligned with the Competency Based Capacity Building (CBCB) framework of Mission Karmayogi . The framework reflects the evolving role of ISS officers in data governance, advanced analytics, emerging technologies, and evidence-based policymaking, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
The report has been prepared through a consultative and evidence-based approach, drawing on the Statistical Training Needs Assessment, existing ISS training programmes, Mission Karmayogi frameworks, international best practices, Committee deliberations, and stakeholder consultations.
The Report presents a future oriented capacity building roadmap comprising three interconnected components. The System of Today , which reviews the existing ISS training ecosystem, capability area practices, and institutional arrangements at National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) . The System of Tomorrow , which establishes a role linked, competency based capacity-building framework covering seven priority capability pillars; and Strategic Recommendations giving actionable measures to transition from current to the envisioned future system to strengthening ISS training, develop future ready competencies, and enhance NSSTA's institutional capacity.
The report outlines an integrated framework comprising the ISS training ecosystem, capability pillars, and institutional architecture. It defines role expectations and assesses the competencies required for each role across functional, domain, and behavioral domains. The framework is to be anchored in the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) , with an emphasis on strengthening human resources, training delivery, and governance to effectively implement training reforms.
Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, complimented the Committee and the NSSTA team for their efforts and comprehensive, forward-looking recommendations. He reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening NSSTA as a pivotal training anchor for Indian Statistical Systems. Implementing these recommendations will directly fortify India's capacity-building structure, ensuring ISS officers remain fully equipped to handle next-generation data requirements and contribute toward the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 .

Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) submitted the Committee's report to Dr. This marks an important milestone toward strengthening the capacity-building framework for ISS officers.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Interacts with Farmers at Kisan Chaupal in Haryana’s Karnal, Calls for Balanced Fertiliser Use and Natural Farming
articles.full_content:
“I am a servant of farmers and will never allow their dignity or the honour of farming to be compromised”: Union Agriculture Minister Farmers should follow Soil Health Cards instead of imitating others when applying fertilisers: Shri Chouhan Natural farming can be profitable when practised correctly; minister shares experience from his own farm Shri Chouhan praises Haryana farmers for improved stubble management and adoption of Super Seeder technology to curb pollution Balanced nutrition, natural farming and improved animal husbandry are key to the future of farmers: Shri Chouhan
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today formally launched the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from the historic town of Taraori in Haryana’s Karnal district. During an interactive Kisan Chaupal organised as part of the campaign, he engaged directly with farmers and stressed that serving the farming community was his highest duty. Shri Chouhan reiterated that, under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, protecting the dignity, honour and self-respect of farmers and farming remained a top priority for the Central Government. Haryana Agriculture Minister Shri Shyam Singh Rana, local legislators, senior agricultural scientists from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI), and a large number of progressive farmers attended the programme.
Opening the interaction, Shri Chouhan said he regarded himself not as a leader holding a high office but as a servant of farmers and a committed farmer himself. “This turban symbolises the honour and self-respect of farmers, and I will never allow it to be lowered. The need of the hour is to bring modern practices and traditional wisdom together in a way that protects our soil while improving farmers’ incomes,” he said.
Follow Soil Health Cards, not the herd mentality, when applying fertilisers
Expressing concern over excessive use of chemical fertilisers, Shri Chouhan clarified that the objective of the Khet Bachao Abhiyan was not to oppose fertilisers indiscriminately but to promote their balanced and scientific use. Explaining the consequences of excessive application, he said that just as taking calcium supplements without a medical need could harm the body, applying chemical fertilisers unnecessarily was damaging soil fertility. He urged farmers to move away from competitive and imitative practices in fertiliser use. “If Ramlal applies four bags of fertiliser, Shyamlal should not feel compelled to apply four and a half bags. Farmers must break free from this tendency to imitate others. First, assess the soil through the Soil Health Card and then provide balanced nutrition according to its actual requirements,” he said. Such an approach would help reduce cultivation costs while protecting soil health for future generations, he added.
